title: Fix Thunderbolt suspend on the MacBookPro14,1
author: orospakr
body:
Enables working lid-close suspend on the 2017 13″ MacBook Pro (MacBookPro14,1), non-Touchbar so no T1. Companion to the `tb-ar-shim-dkms` package PR in omarchy-pkgs; full investigation in #10593.

**The problem:** every suspend breaks Thunderbolt on this machine — two Linux PCI bugs (garbage config-space restore after S3; skipped restore on s2idle), plus an Apple EFI behavior where entering S3 with anything in a Thunderbolt port makes the firmware disable the Thunderbolt root port until the next **cold boot**. The EFI part is unfixable from the OS, which is why the machine must default to s2idle (s2idle never executes the EFI S3 resume script).

**What this adds:**

- `bin/omarchy-hw-macbookpro14-1` — detector: exact DMI product match + `lspci` check for the Alpine Ridge bridge (8086:1578). Gates on 14,1 alone because that's the validated machine; 14,2/14,3 share the controller and can be added once tested.
- `install/hardware/apple/fix-thunderbolt-suspend.sh` (+ `all.sh` entry) — installs `linux-headers` + `tb-ar-shim-dkms`, loads the module immediately (the modalias coldplug has already passed on a live system), and writes a limine cmdline drop-in with `mem_sleep_default=s2idle` (the `fix-t2.sh` mechanism).
- `migrations/1788811585.sh` — same for already-installed machines, with the `limine-mkinitcpio` rebuild guard so the cmdline reaches the boot entries.

**Validation:** this exact flow ran end-to-end on a MacBookPro14,1 — package install, dkms build, detector match, drop-in + UKI rebuild, then a cold boot: module autoloaded by modalias, `mem_sleep` came up `[s2idle]`, and suspend cycles are clean at ~1.3 s resume (vs 75–107 s with dead Thunderbolt before). `test/shell` passes (the two failures on this machine, locate/snapper, pre-exist on master).

**Depends on** the omarchy-pkgs PR publishing `tb-ar-shim-dkms` — draft until that lands.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,8 @@
+#!/bin/bash
+
+# omarchy:summary=Match the Apple MacBook Pro 14,1 (13-inch 2017, no Touch Bar) with its Alpine Ridge Thunderbolt controller.
+
+product_name="${OMARCHY_DMI_PRODUCT_NAME:-/sys/class/dmi/id/product_name}"
+
+grep -qix "MacBookPro14,1" "$product_name" 2>/dev/null &&
+  lspci -n 2>/dev/null | grep -q "8086:1578"

@@ -0,0 +1,45 @@
+# The 2017 13" MacBook Pro (MacBookPro14,1) breaks Thunderbolt on every
+# lid-close suspend. Three separate causes, two of them Linux bugs, one Apple
+# firmware behavior (details: https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/10593):
+#
+#  - In the default deep (S3) sleep the PCI core saves the Alpine Ridge
+#    bridges' config space after the thunderbolt driver has already put the
+#    chip to sleep, so resume restores garbage: 75-107 s wakeups, dead
+#    Thunderbolt and USB-C.
+#  - Entering S3 with anything plugged into a Thunderbolt port makes the
+#    Mac's EFI resume script disable the Thunderbolt root port entirely;
+#    only a cold boot brings it back. No kernel change can prevent this,
+#    which is why the machine must default to s2idle.
+#  - In s2idle the PCI core skips config-space restore (skip_bus_pm), but
+#    this controller genuinely loses its config space during sleep, so it
+#    comes back dead there too.
+#
+# tb-ar-shim-dkms fixes the two kernel-side bugs (config saved early, restored
+# on resume; being submitted upstream as PCI quirks), and the limine drop-in
+# makes s2idle the default sleep mode so the EFI path can never fire.
+# Validated on MacBookPro14,1: 28/28 suspend cycles, 1.3 s resume.
+# MacBookPro14,2/14,3 share the controller but are unvalidated, so this gates
+# on the exact model.
+
+if omarchy-hw-macbookpro14-1; then
+  echo "Detected MacBookPro14,1; fixing Thunderbolt suspend"
+
+  omarchy-pkg-add linux-headers tb-ar-shim-dkms
+
+  # The module autoloads by PCI modalias at boot, but on a live system that
+  # coldplug event has already passed — load it now so the first suspend
+  # after this script is already protected.
+  sudo modprobe tb_ar_shim || true
+
+  sudo mkdir -p /etc/limine-entry-tool.d
+  sudo tee /etc/limine-entry-tool.d/macbookpro14-1-thunderbolt.conf >/dev/null <<'EOF'
+# Generated by Omarchy installer for MacBookPro14,1 Thunderbolt support.
+# Deep (S3) sleep with a Thunderbolt device attached lets the Mac's EFI
+# resume script disable the Thunderbolt root port until the next cold boot;
+# s2idle never runs that script.
+KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" mem_sleep_default=s2idle"
+EOF
+
+  # Take effect before the next reboot too
+  echo s2idle | sudo tee /sys/power/mem_sleep >/dev/null || true
+fi

@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+# Fix Thunderbolt suspend on the MacBookPro14,1: install the tb-ar-shim DKMS
+# module and default the machine to s2idle sleep, then rebuild boot images so
+# the cmdline change reaches the Limine entries.
+# Same logic as install/hardware/apple/fix-thunderbolt-suspend.sh; see
+# https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/issues/10593 for the investigation.
+
+if omarchy-hw-macbookpro14-1; then
+  echo "Detected MacBookPro14,1; fixing Thunderbolt suspend"
+
+  omarchy-pkg-add linux-headers tb-ar-shim-dkms
+
+  # The module autoloads by PCI modalias at boot, but on a live system that
+  # coldplug event has already passed — load it now so the first suspend
+  # after this migration is already protected.
+  sudo modprobe tb_ar_shim || true
+
+  sudo mkdir -p /etc/limine-entry-tool.d
+  sudo tee /etc/limine-entry-tool.d/macbookpro14-1-thunderbolt.conf >/dev/null <<'EOF'
+# Generated by Omarchy installer for MacBookPro14,1 Thunderbolt support.
+# Deep (S3) sleep with a Thunderbolt device attached lets the Mac's EFI
+# resume script disable the Thunderbolt root port until the next cold boot;
+# s2idle never runs that script.
+KERNEL_CMDLINE[default]+=" mem_sleep_default=s2idle"
+EOF
+
+  # Take effect before the reboot too
+  echo s2idle | sudo tee /sys/power/mem_sleep >/dev/null || true
+
+  if ! grep -q "mem_sleep_default=s2idle" /proc/cmdline; then
+    if command -v limine-mkinitcpio >/dev/null 2>&1; then
+      sudo limine-mkinitcpio
+    fi
+  fi
+fi
